title: Pots and pans
hook: Brother Lawrence, a Carmelite cook, turning an omelette for the love of God

segments.voice: Yesterday, the living flame: John's fire that turns a damp log into glow. Your line was o living flame. Did something sting today that might have been the good kind of fire? Day one thousand one hundred thirty-eight.

A monastery kitchen in Paris. Steam, noise, people calling for things all at once. At the stove stands a lay brother of the Carmelites, a former soldier, by his own account clumsy, who says he had a great dislike for kitchen work. His name in religion is Brother Lawrence of the Resurrection. He didn't leave a big book. What we have is some of his letters and the notes of a priest who visited him and wrote down their conversations. They were published after his death, and in English they're known by a title that stuck: The Practice of the Presence of God. And the scene people remember isn't in a chapel. It's at the stove, with a pan. Today: pots and pans.
screen: `THE PRACTICE OF THE PRESENCE OF GOD.`

segments.voice: Lawrence's secret, as he told it, was almost embarrassingly simple. He would turn the little cake frying in the pan for the love of God. When it was done, if there was nothing else to do, he'd bow down and thank God, and then get up again, happier than a king. He'd pick a piece of straw off the ground, for the love of God. The task didn't matter. What mattered was who he did it for. He said that for him the time of work didn't differ from the time of prayer. In the noise and clatter of his kitchen, with several people calling for different things, he said he had God as calmly as if he were on his knees before the sacrament. That's the whole teaching: not a technique, a habit of turning toward God in the middle of things, and turning back again whenever you notice you've wandered off. He wasn't hard on himself about the wandering. When he forgot, he admitted it, and came back. Paul had said it long before: "And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men." And again: "whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God." Lawrence just took Paul at his word, in a kitchen. Two days ago we stood on John's mountain of nothing. Yesterday, his flame. Lawrence belongs to the same family, and he brings it down to the stove. The holy place, for him, was wherever his hands were.
screen: `TURN THE CAKE FOR THE LOVE OF GOD.`
`WHATSOEVER YE DO, AS TO THE LORD.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: plan something to cook, or make, for love. Sit and breathe. Think of the next ordinary thing your hands will do today: making coffee, a sandwich, folding a towel, washing a pan. Picture yourself doing it slowly, all the way through. Now decide who it's for. If you pray, you can do it for the love of God, the way Lawrence turned his cake. If you don't, do it for someone you love, or simply with full attention. Let the plain task be enough. The bell holds the time.
Pots and pans. Brother Lawrence's kitchen, where turning a cake for the love of God was as much prayer as kneeling in church.
Your line: turn it for love. Today, pick one dull chore and do it as if it were a gift, for God or for someone, and notice if it changes the chore. Day one thousand one hundred thirty-eight.

howItsDone: Christians across churches read Brother Lawrence's The Practice of the Presence of God and try to keep a simple awareness of God through ordinary work, turning back to God briefly and often during the day.

quietly turn back to God, right there at the stove.

notes: Brother Lawrence is paraphrased throughout (public-domain English translations exist but are not on the validator's list): turning the 'little omelette'/'cake' in the pan for the love of God; picking up straw; 'the time of business does not with me differ from the time of prayer'; the noise and clatter of the kitchen; 'as if upon my knees at the blessed sacrament'; 'happier than a king'. Confirm each is in the Letters or Conversations.
Hook: Paris monastery, lay brother, former soldier, clumsy, 'a great dislike' of kitchen work: from the Conversations (Abbé de Beaufort). Confirm. No dates or ages given.
'A handful of his letters' and 'published after his death' are general; confirm or soften.
'His name in religion is Brother Lawrence of the Resurrection' — confirm.
howItsDone: 'Christians across churches' refers to readership across denominations; confirm.
Editor (2026-10-02): 'a handful of his letters' (a count claim) changed to 'some of his letters' in the hook and myth.
Auditor (2026-10-02): the French originals (1692–94) were not titled 'The Practice of the Presence of God'; that is the later English title. Hook and trapdoor now say it is the English title.
